pictures.scene: Repin, Religious Procession in Kursk Province — a whole countryside is on the move along a wide dusty road under a hazy summer sky, the gilded banners of the procession carried up high in the distance with the jewelled shrine glittering between them in the dust and heat, the road behind packed solid with heads as far as the eye can see, a priest in a stiff gold brocade vestment walking at the right with his hair and beard catching the sun, a stout lady in a cream flounced dress holding the icon out in front of her with both hands and the gentlemen in black coats pressing close around her, mounted police at the left edge keeping the lane open, a crippled boy in a long grey coat driving himself forward on his crutch at the front with his lame leg swinging and his face set hard, the bare trampled sandhill rising beyond with its trees cut away, soon afterward, jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of god, the twelve were with him, as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, mary called magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out
pictures.name: pd_repin_religious_procession_in_kursk_province

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching at Athens — the apostle stands alone on the top step of a great classical hall in a sea-green tunic with a heavy rose-red mantle wound round him and falling to his bare feet, both arms thrown straight up above his head and his bearded face turned in profile as he speaks, a thin gold halo behind his hair, the listeners seated and standing on the steps below him on either side, an old man in a red cap and a blue-green cloak looking up at him with his mouth set and his hands clasped on his knee, a young man at the left leaning his chin on his fist in thought, a curly-headed boy staring straight out from behind the column, two men at the right half turned away to argue it over between themselves, the deep arched bays and the tall fluted pilasters of the building rising behind on every side and the pale paved floor spread out empty in front, joanna the wife of herod's household manager chuza, susanna, and many others, these women were ministering to them out of their own means, while a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to jesus from town after town, he told them this parable
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_paul_preaching_at_athens

pictures.scene: Millet, The Sower — a labourer strides down the broken slope of a ploughed field at dusk scattering seed with a wide swing of his arm, his whole body thrown forward into the stride and his right hand flung out and open with the grain already gone from it, the left hand digging into the mouth of the heavy seed bag slung across his chest and knotted at his hip, a soft dark hat pulled down so that his face is in shadow under the brim, a worn red-brown jacket and a blue smock and faded blue trousers bound about with rags at the ankles, his boots sunk into the loose dark earth, the ridged furrows running away up the hill behind him and a pale cold sky above with a last streak of light along the horizon, a sunlit bank and a team working in the far distance at the right, a farmer went out to sow his seed, and as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it, some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_sower

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Harvesters — a field of ripe corn stands uncut and shining at the left while the mown half runs away gold and stubbled to the trees, a big pear tree growing up through the middle of the picture with its branches spread over everything, the reapers resting at noon in the shade under it, one man flat on his back asleep in the stubble with his legs sprawled and his shirt open, another tipping a brown jug up to drink, a woman in a white cap eating from a bowl with her spoon, a man in a straw hat cutting the loaf on a white cloth and his neighbour reaching into the basket for the jar, men in wide hats sitting round with their bowls at the right, a woman going off down the cut lane with a sheaf on her shoulder and another bending to bind one, the conical stooks standing in rows across the field, a church spire and the hedges and the far country showing between the trees beyond, other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings, still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop, a hundredfold, as jesus said this, he called out, he who has ears to hear, let him hear
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_harvesters

pictures.scene: Veronese, Christ Among the Doctors in the Temple — the boy sits up on the high marble ledge of the temple in a rose-pink tunic with a dark blue-green mantle over His knees and one bare sandalled foot hanging down, one hand lifted with the first finger up as He makes the point and the other turned open and out toward the men below, His young face calm and His fair hair falling in curls, the learned men crowded up the steps underneath Him at the left, one in a yellow robe with a great clasped book open on his lap, a bald one with his hand spread on his chest leaning forward to object, a grey-bearded elder at the right hand side holding his book half shut and arguing back across the rail, women in white veils watching from a gallery behind, an hourglass standing on the stone bench with the sand running and a dog stretched out asleep on the floor below, the grooved pilasters and the carved cornice of the temple going up into shadow over everything, then his disciples asked him what this parable meant, he replied, the knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of god has been given to you, but to others i speak in parables, so that, though seeing, they may not see, though hearing, they may not understand
pictures.name: pd_veronese_doctors

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, Still Life with Open Bible — a great family Bible lies open on the table with its heavy dark leather boards spread flat and its thick block of pages fanned out, the two open pages painted in broad strokes of cream and ochre with the double column of print only suggested and the chapter number set in at the top, the brass clasps and the worn edges of the binding catching what light there is, a tall turned brass candlestick standing behind it with a stub of candle burnt right down and the wick dead, a small cheap yellow paperback lying face up in front with its covers curled and its title showing, the heavy cloth of the table rucked up under everything in brown and gold, the whole room behind sunk in flat black, now this is the meaning of the parable, the seed is the word of god, the seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved
pictures.name: pd_gogh_bijbel

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — an old man sits alone at night in a crowded counting room holding a single candle up close to his face, the flame hidden behind his curled fingers so that the whole light of the picture comes through his hand and burns red through the skin, his spectacles pushed down his nose and his lips parted as he squints at the paper he has lifted into the light, a fur-lined black cap set back on his bald head and a wide pleated ruff and a gold-braided chain across his breast, a bulging leather money bag slumped on the shelf beside him with its strings loose and a dagger hanging above it, stacks of ledgers and bundles of sealed papers piled up at the right into the shadow, a little heap of gold coins and a pair of hand scales lying on the table below in front of him, the rest of the room sunk away into brown dark, the seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root, they believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away, the seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_parable_of_the_rich_fool

pictures.scene: Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ stands at night outside a long-shut door in an overgrown orchard, a white robe falling to His bare feet with a heavy jewelled clasp and breastplate at the breast and a dark gold-worked mantle over His shoulders, a crown of thorns set on His head with a thin gold halo burning behind it, His bearded face turned quietly out of the picture and His right hand lifted to knock at the boards, a many-sided lantern hung from His left hand with the candle alight inside it and the little star and crescent holes throwing their light down over the weeds, the door itself grown shut with ivy and rusted at the hinges with no handle on the outside at all, nettles and brambles and fallen apples thick across the sill, the bare branches of the orchard crossing against a deep blue night sky, but the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop, no one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed, instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: Antonello da Messina, Saint Jerome in His Study — the whole inside of a great hall is laid open to the eye through one carved stone arch, with a wooden study built like a little stage in the middle of the tiled floor, the scholar sitting up on it in a red robe and a red cap with his slippers left off on the step below, holding an open book propped on the reading desk and turned in strict profile to the page, his shelves running away behind him stacked with volumes lying flat and standing on end and a jar and a box and a folded cloth among them, the ribbed vault and the tall windows showing the pale sky above, a lion walking quietly up the arcade at the right in the shadow and a cat curled asleep on the ledge at the left, a peacock and a partridge and a brass basin set out along the stone sill at the very front, for there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light, pay attention, therefore, to how you listen, whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him
pictures.name: pd_antonello_saint_jerome_in_his_study

pictures.scene: Neuhuys, Mother and Child — a young mother sits on a plain rush chair in a bare brown cottage room holding her baby on her lap, a white linen cap over her hair and a worn olive jacket and a heavy dark blue skirt falling to the floor, her head bent right down over the child and her face quiet and half in shadow, one hand holding the little one steady by the knee and the other arm round behind to keep him up, the child in a short white shift with his bare legs hanging down and one knitted bootee still on, turning a small rattle over in his fist and looking down at it, a round wicker basket of mending standing on the table at the left with the handle up, the floor dark and empty in front of them and the rough plaster wall rising bare behind, then jesus' mother and brothers came to see him, but they were unable to reach him because of the crowd, he was told, your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you
pictures.name: pd_neuhuys_moeder_en_kind

pictures.scene: Tintoretto, Christ at the Sea of Galilee — Christ stands alone on the rocky shore seen from behind and in lost profile, a steel blue tunic across His shoulders and a long rose-pink mantle wound about His waist and falling in heavy folds to the ground, a thin halo of light behind His red-brown hair, His right arm stretched straight out and the first finger pointing away across the water to the far shore, the lake running out from His feet in long white-crested rollers driven by the wind, a dark headland of rock and scrub between Him and the open water with a bare tree twisting out of it, the low green and grey hills of the far side lit in streaks under a sky piled with black and silver storm cloud and torn open at the top, a stunted tree leaning in at the left edge, but he replied, my mother and brothers are those who hear the word of god and carry it out, one day jesus said to his disciples, let us cross to the other side of the lake, so he got into a boat with them and set out
pictures.name: pd_tintoretto_galilee

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee — a small fishing boat is stood almost on end by a wave that has broken clean over the bow, the mast and the rigging thrown across the whole picture at a steep slant and the torn sail half pulled down, one man up at the bowsprit hanging on to the forestay with both hands and his face turned up to the sky, another clinging over the side with his cap gone, a man in yellow on his knees in the bilge gripping a rope and shouting, white spray and green water boiling up over the left gunwale into the boat, a sailor at the stern heaving on the tiller with his whole weight, and down in the dark of the stern Christ sitting quietly upright in the midst of them with His hands on His knee and His face calm as one disciple leans right over Him and takes Him by the arm to wake Him, another doubled up and sick at the rail below, the black storm sky piled over everything with one burst of gold light in the cloud at the left, as they sailed, he fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger, the disciples went and woke him, saying, master, master, we are perishing, then jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_christ_in_the_storm_on_the_sea_of_galilee

pictures.scene: Kensett, Lake George — the lake lies out perfectly still after the weather has gone through, the water a sheet of pale silver with the whole mountain reflected in it without a ripple, a long wooded ridge coming down from the right in blue shadow with the morning light running along its flank in streaks of green and gold, a smaller headland of firs behind it and the far shore fading away into the haze at the end of the lake, a little rocky island at the left with three or four wind-bent trees standing on it and its reflection hanging under it, a shelf of lichened brown rock in the near corner with grass and a few small flowers growing out of the cracks and the reeds standing up out of the shallow water beside it, the sky above hazed over to a soft pearl with the last of the broken cloud dissolving at the top and a thin line of birds crossing it, where is your faith, he asked, frightened and amazed, they asked one another, who is this, he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him, then they sailed to the region of the gerasenes, across the lake from galilee
pictures.name: pd_kensett_lake

pictures.scene: Bermejo, Saint Michael Triumphant over the Devil — the archangel stands straight over the beast in a full suit of polished gold armour worked with pearls at every joint, his sword swung right up behind his head in both hands ready to come down, his young face calm and the eyes lowered, great feathered wings of orange and crimson spread out behind him and a crimson mantle lined with gold brocade flying up and filling the whole upper half of the panel, a crystal shield held on his left arm, his pointed gold shoes set on the body of the devil beneath him, the devil a scaled grey monster with horns and red staring eyes set all over its armoured back, its jaws open wide and its clawed feet thrown up in the air, a donor in a black cap and a silver damask gown kneeling small at the left with his open book held up in both hands and his face lifted toward the angel, the whole ground behind them beaten gold, when jesus stepped ashore, he was met by a demon-possessed man from the town, for a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs, when the man saw jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, shouting in a loud voice, what do you want with me, jesus, son of the most high god, i beg you not to torture me
pictures.name: pd_bermejo_saint_michael_triumphant_over_the_devil

pictures.scene: Veronese, The Pleading Before the Guard — an old man in a blue mantle leans down out of the shadow of a stone doorway with his face drawn and his hand held out open in appeal, an old woman kneeling at his knee in a fur-trimmed cloak and a white veil with her head bowed and her mouth set, a second woman behind her looking up in distress and a boy in a red jacket crouching against her skirts with his face turned out, the soldiers standing over against them in a close group at the right, one in a steel helmet with a thick blue plume and a great green cloak slung across his shoulder turning his hand over as he answers, a heavy bearded officer behind him in a gold gorget looking away, a young captain at the edge in red armour and gilded straps with his face set hard, a white marble balustrade running behind them with women and children leaning over it to watch and more faces crowded in the archway below, the pale wall of the building going up into a quiet sky, for jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man, many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places, what is your name, jesus asked, legion, he replied, because many demons had gone into him
pictures.name: pd_veronese_ketenen

pictures.scene: Cuyp, Young Herdsmen with Cows — a herd is lying out on the top of a low rise in the late afternoon, a big black cow standing broadside across the middle of the picture with its back catching the light, three or four red and dun cattle couched in the dry grass in front of it chewing with their horned heads turned different ways, more of the herd bedded down along the ridge behind, two young herdsmen standing together up at the right among them, one in a brown coat and a flat black cap talking and pointing with his hand, the other in a broad straw hat and a blue jerkin leaning on a long staff and listening, the ground running down into shadow at the front with burdock leaves and a tangle of brambles growing over it, a great bank of grey and silver cloud filling the sky above with a shaft of light breaking through it at the left and a single bird on the wing, and the demons kept begging jesus not to order them to go into the abyss, there on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding, so the demons begged jesus to let them enter the pigs, and he gave them permission
pictures.name: pd_cuyp_young_herdsmen_with_cows

pictures.scene: Ruisdael, A Waterfall — a river comes down off the high ground in a single steep drop and bursts into white water at the bottom of the picture, the whole fall thrown over a ledge of dark rock in two broad sheets that meet and boil up together, loose boulders standing in the middle of the stream with the water driving round them and the foam running out over the stones at the very front, a great mass of brown rock rising at the left with an oak grown half out of it and bent over the drop, a smaller red-leaved tree below it and the bank behind thick with wood, the river coming down in broken rapids out of the distance, a bare green mountain standing up beyond the trees with its summit catching the light, a tall bank of white cloud piled up in the grey sky above it, then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned, when those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_a_waterfall

pictures.scene: Eastman Johnson, The Lord Is My Shepherd — a man sits alone on a low seat in the corner of a dark bare room with a small book open across his knee, both hands holding it steady and his head bent right down over the page, his face quiet and absorbed with the light coming across his cheek and his short hair, a loose white shirt with the sleeves rolled back over his wrists and the collar open, a dark waistcoat and dark trousers and heavy worn boots set flat on the bare boards, a yellow kerchief hanging down inside the collar, the planks of a red wooden door standing at the left edge and the wall behind him sunk away into deep red-brown shadow, a bundle and a few things lying on the floor beside him in the dark, so the people went out to see what had happened, they came to jesus and found the man whom the demons had left, sitting at jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid, meanwhile, those who had seen it reported how the demon-possessed man had been healed
pictures.name: pd_johnson_the_lord_is_my_shepherd

pictures.scene: Cole, The Departure — a company is riding out from a castle on a summer morning, the great battlemented keep standing up on its wooded crag at the right with its towers and its flag and the long wall and viaduct running back into the hill, a stone gate tower below it with a banner flying from the roof and spearmen standing on the parapet, the riders coming down over the arched bridge in a line with their lances up and their pennons out, a knight on a white horse at the head of them and his squires behind, a herald in red riding out under the trees at the left, a broad green meadow sloping down in front with a great oak spreading over it and goats lying in its shade, a hermit in a brown habit standing alone at the bottom of the slope with his staff in one hand and the other raised after them, the river running out under the bridge over its stones, blue mountains going back range behind range into the haze with a white waterfall coming off one of them and a sunlit cloud bank above, then all the people of the region of the gerasenes asked jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them, so he got into the boat and started back, the man whom the demons had left begged to go with jesus, but he sent him away, saying
pictures.name: pd_cole_the_departure

pictures.scene: Burnand, Come Home Again — an old father stands in the doorway of his house and takes his son back, the two of them filling the whole picture, the father in a long pale robe with a heavy cream mantle over his shoulder, his white hair and his long grey beard falling forward and his eyes closed as he bends his head down over the boy, one worn hand laid flat on the back of the son's head and the other hand caught up against his own breast, the son fallen in against him with his face buried in the old man's beard and his eyes shut, a coarse dark brown tunic torn at the shoulder and belted at the waist, his bare arm hanging straight down and the hand open and empty at his side, the plain light wall and the stone door jamb of the house rising behind them, return home and describe how much god has done for you, so the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much jesus had done for him, when jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they had all been waiting for him
pictures.name: pd_burnand_thuisgekomen

pictures.scene: Hofmann, Christ and the Rich Young Ruler — Christ stands at the left against a plain stone wall in a dull red tunic with a deep blue-green mantle hanging from His shoulder, His face turned quietly toward the young man beside Him and His eyes steady, His bare arm reaching out and the open hand held low toward him, the young man standing close in at the right in a magnificent cream mantle worked with gold at the border, a turquoise silk sleeve showing under it and an embroidered sash at his waist, a jewelled turban wound over his dark hair, his head bent down and turned away with the eyelids lowered and his mouth shut, his hands clasped together in front of him, the wall behind them bare and dim and the whole weight of the picture in the two faces, just then a synagogue leader named jairus came and fell at jesus' feet, he begged him to come to his house, because his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying, as jesus went with him, the crowds pressed around him
pictures.name: pd_hofmann_christ_and_the_rich_young_ruler

pictures.scene: Carracci, Christ and the Canaanite Woman — a woman has gone down on her knees in the road at the left with her head thrown back and turned up toward Christ, her face lit and her mouth open as she keeps asking, a pale sleeve and a blue bodice and a great fall of golden drapery over her lap and her bare feet, one hand reaching out low in front of her and the other held up at her throat, Christ standing over against her at the right in a deep blue mantle gathered up in His left hand with a red tunic showing under it, His bare feet set firm on the paved road and His bearded head bent down toward her, His right hand come out from under the cloak with the fingers open and almost touching hers, the dark walls and the round tower of a town rising behind them with trees over the roofs and a few small figures in the archway below, including a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years, she had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her, she came up behind jesus and touched the fringe of his cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped
pictures.name: pd_carracci_canaanite_woman

pictures.scene: Poussin, Saints Peter and John Healing the Lame Man — two apostles stand together on the temple steps in the middle of a press of people, the younger one at the left in a sea-green tunic with a rose-pink mantle falling from his shoulder, his fair head bent down and his right arm thrown straight up with the first finger pointing at the sky while his left hand is held out open and low to the beggar below, the older one beside him in a heavy ochre cloak over a blue robe, bald and red-bearded and looking away over his shoulder with his hand resting on his knee, the lame man down on the stone at the bottom left with his wasted bare legs stretched out and his thin arm reaching up, a bearded man in a brown tunic and a blue cloak crowding in behind them and others pushing from both sides, the long white courses of the temple wall going up behind and a bright blue sky above it with white cloud, who touched me, jesus asked, but they all denied it, master, said peter, the people are crowding and pressing against you, but jesus declared, someone touched me, for i know that power has gone out from me
pictures.name: pd_poussin_healing_lame_man

pictures.scene: Maes, An Old Woman Praying — an old woman sits alone at the corner of her table with her hands folded tight together and lifted in front of her, her head up and turned a little away and her eyes open and fixed on something out of the picture, the lines deep in her cheek and her mouth drawn, a small white lace cap tied under her hair and a stiff white linen collar at her throat, a plain black jacket with the sleeves to the wrist, a heavy striped curtain hanging down behind her shoulder in brown and gold, the table in front covered with a thick red cloth and a large open book lying on it with the pages flat, a pair of round spectacles and a quill laid across the page and a little brass inkstand beside them, a cushion and a chair back at the left and the room behind her gone almost black, then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before him, in the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched him and how she had immediately been healed, daughter, said jesus, your faith has healed you, go in peace
pictures.name: pd_maes_an_old_woman_praying

pictures.scene: Heyerdahl, The Dying Child — a sick child lies on a white pillow in a low bed in a poor room gone almost entirely dark, the small face turned up and the eyes half closed and one little hand laid out flat on the sheet, a white embroidered coverlet drawn up over the body and a pale blanket folded under, the mother bent right down over the bedhead in a dark dress with her face close above the child and her shoulder blocking the light, the father standing apart at the left in a dark coat with his hand pressed against his mouth and his head turned away, a younger sister standing at the foot of the bed in a long white nightshirt with her back to us and her hair loose, a tall woman waiting in shadow along the right side of the room, one small red lamp burning on the wall behind them and everything else sunk in brown, while he was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader, your daughter is dead, he told jairus, do not bother the teacher anymore, but jesus overheard them and said to jairus, do not be afraid, just believe, and she will be healed
pictures.name: pd_heyerdahl_dying_child

pictures.scene: Bendemann, The Mourning Jews in Exile — an old man sits on the ground under a vine-hung tree in a long dull red robe with a deep ochre turban wound round his head and a short cape of the same cloth over his shoulders, his white beard spread over his chest and his face turned away to the left with his eyes lowered and his mouth set, an iron shackle locked on his wrist with a heavy chain hanging from it down across his knee, his hand resting slack on the frame of a wooden harp that is laid over on its side on the grass with the strings untouched, a young woman fallen across his lap with her hair in a plaited golden coil and her face hidden in his robe and her bare arms thrown over her head, her own hand clasped against her hair, green vine leaves and a rough trunk filling the whole upper part behind them and a sliver of pale sky at the left, when he entered the house, he did not allow anyone to go in with him except peter, john, james, and the child's father and mother, meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her, but jesus said, stop weeping, she is not dead but asleep
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_jews_mourning_in_exile

pictures.scene: De Wet, Christ Blessing the Children — Christ sits on a low step in the shadowed doorway of a great stone building in a plain pale robe with a dull red mantle across His knees, a faint ring of light round His head, His face bent down and His hand laid against His own breast as He looks at the children brought to Him, a young mother kneeling at the left in a blue skirt and a white bodice with an orange sash holding her baby forward on her arm, a small boy in grey standing at Christ's knee with his face turned up, a girl in a yellow dress and a striped headcloth kneeling on the step in front of Him with her hands together, a toddler in a cap being helped along at the right, another boy in a red cap crouching on the bare ground in the foreground with his back to us, a bearded old man standing watching from the shadow behind and more faces crowded in at both sides, and they laughed at him, knowing that she was dead, but jesus took her by the hand and called out, child, get up
pictures.name: pd_dewet_christus_zegent_kinderen

pictures.scene: Vermeer, The Milkmaid — a serving woman stands at a table in the corner of a plain whitewashed kitchen pouring milk in a thin unbroken stream from a brown earthenware jug down into a wide stoneware bowl, her head bent over the work and her eyes on the stream, a stiff white linen cap folded back over her hair and a white collar at her neck, a yellow bodice laced down the front with the blue sleeves pushed up above her strong bare forearms, a thick blue apron tied over a dull red skirt, the table in front of her covered with a blue cloth and loaded with a basket of broken bread and a crusty loaf and a blue and white jug, a wicker basket and a copper pail hanging on nails on the bare wall behind her and a small window at the far left letting in the only light, her spirit returned, and at once she got up, and he directed that she be given something to eat, her parents were astounded, but jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened
pictures.name: pd_vermeer_the_milkmaid

lines.text: Soon afterward, Jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with Him,
as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
Joanna the wife of Herod's household manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others. These women were ministering to them out of their own means.
While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from town after town, He told them this parable:
A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.
Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.
Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.
Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop, a hundredfold. As Jesus said this, He called out, He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
Then His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.

He replied, The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that, though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand.
Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.
The seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.
The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.
But the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.
Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.
Then Jesus' mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd.
He was told, Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.
But He replied, My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.
One day Jesus said to His disciples, Let us cross to the other side of the lake. So He got into a boat with them and set out.
As they sailed, He fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.
The disciples went and woke Him, saying, Master, Master, we are perishing! Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm.
Where is your faith? He asked. Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!
Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
When Jesus stepped ashore, He was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs.
When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!

For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places.
What is your name? Jesus asked. Legion, he replied, because many demons had gone into him.
And the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss.
There on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding. So the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs, and He gave them permission.
Then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside.
So the people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man whom the demons had left, sitting at Jesus' feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
Meanwhile, those who had seen it reported how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
Then all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them. So He got into the boat and started back.
The man whom the demons had left begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away, saying,
Return home and describe how much God has done for you. So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been waiting for Him.
Just then a synagogue leader named Jairus came and fell at Jesus' feet. He begged Him to come to his house,
because his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying. As Jesus went with him, the crowds pressed around Him,
including a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her.
She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
Who touched Me? Jesus asked. But they all denied it. Master, said Peter, the people are crowding and pressing against You.
But Jesus declared, Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.

Then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before Him. In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.
Daughter, said Jesus, your faith has healed you. Go in peace.
While He was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader. Your daughter is dead, he told Jairus. Do not bother the Teacher anymore.
But Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.
When He entered the house, He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child's father and mother.
Meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.
And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead.
But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, Child, get up!
Her spirit returned, and at once she got up. And He directed that she be given something to eat.
Her parents were astounded, but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
